subject: Eval materials consignment: datasets + prompt packs — MAP & acceptance gates
messages:
From: Emma Zhao <emma@catalyst.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@catalyst.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Eval materials consignment: datasets & prompt packs

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for taking the time last week — really excited to move into an evaluation phase with Redwood. Per our discussion, Catalyst.ai is prepared to consignment a scoped set of testcases, a ~10k-sample evaluation dataset (anonymized), and a prompt pack for model coverage testing. Before we ship anything we'd like to align on a Mutual Action Plan and the usage constraints:

High-level asks from our side:
- Ephemeral access (30-day TTL) for the dataset and prompt pack; no redistribution outside of Redwood.
- Audit logging for every access (who/when) and a daily access summary during the trial.
- A canary acceptance window: 5 business days for functional smoke tests, then a 10 business day quality review.
- Confirm handling of gradients/outputs (we'd prefer outputs not be stored persistently for >7 days).

We can provide the materials via a signed S3 presigned URL or encrypted archive. Attached is a brief index of the proposed deliverables (manifest). Can you confirm the gate criteria you need on your side and who should be on the MAP?

Best,
Emma Zhao
Head of Partnerships | Catalyst.ai
[Attachment: manifest-summary.txt]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Emma Zhao <emma@catalyst.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@catalyst.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Eval materials consignment: datasets & prompt packs

Hi Emma — thanks, this looks straightforward and we appreciate the clear asks. I pulled together a short Mutual Action Plan draft and attached it (mutual-action-plan-CAT-20261116.pdf). Typos aside, the MAP proposes:

1) Deliverables
- Catalyst provides: eval-dataset (10k anonymized records), prompt-pack-v1 (structured prompts and expected labels), testcase-suite (200 targeted cases).
- Redwood provides: dedicated ephemeral sandbox, access logs, evaluation runbook, and weekly syncs.

2) Acceptance gates
- Canary: Redwood runs smoke harness against 50 samples within 48 hours of ingest.
- Quality: Redwood provides a quality report (accuracy/coverage) within 10 business days.
- A joint acceptance signoff to transition to the pilot phase.

3) Usage constraints (drafted)
- No redistribution, no derivative dataset sharing.
- Outputs persisted only for debugging up to 7 days unless otherwise agreed.
- Access TTL default 30 days; extension by written request.

4) Operational steps & timeline
- Day 0: Contract NDAs & S3 transfer.
- Day 1–2: Canary ingestion.
- Day 3–14: Full run & quality assessment.

Can Marissa and Karthik confirm if the MAP needs further security clauses (retention, encryption, audit cadence) before we sign? We'll include a DocuSign link once we lock the bullets.

Thanks — attaching the MAP draft for review.

Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: mutual-action-plan-CAT-20261116.pdf]

Subject: Re: Eval materials consignment: datasets & prompt packs — security notes

Jordan / team — quick security and compliance notes to include in the MAP before we sign:

- Access provisioning: must be scoped to named Redwood accounts (no generic shared credentials). Use short-lived STS tokens tied to SSO.
- Audit logging: immutable logs (WORM) for access events during the trial window, with a daily summary pushed to Catalyst; logs retained for 90 days by default.
- Encryption: dataset-at-rest encrypted with customer-managed KMS key; transfer via presigned S3 over TLS.
- Data lifecycle: dataset must be trashed & overwritten at destruction; provide a cryptographic checksum & destruction confirmation (signed) on expiry.
- Output handling: enforce a 7-day retention default for model outputs; any retention >7 days requires Catalyst written approval.
- Watermarking/traceability: include an internal run-id in outputs to help forensics in the unlikely event of leakage.

I attached a short security checklist appendix. We should also get a legal redline if Catalyst wants different retention windows. Once we have alignment we'll send the DocuSign envelope.

-- Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Security Integrations | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: security-checklist-redwood-appendix.pdf]

Subject: Re: Eval materials consignment: datasets & prompt packs — final MAP & schedule

Emma / Samir — thanks for the patience while we tightened the MAP. Catalyst items look good; we can agree to the constraints with the following concrete operational commitments on Redwood's side:

Delivery & access
- Catalyst will upload to a pre-agreed S3 bucket and share an encrypted archive. We will provision short-lived SSO-bound access for the named engineers. Expected transfer window: 11/30–12/01.

Canary & acceptance cadence
- Day 0 (ingest): Redwood runs a 50-sample canary within 48 hours.
- Day 3–12: Full evaluation run and automated metrics report (accuracy, hallucination rate, prompt coverage).
- Day 13–15: Joint quality review and signoff or a maximum of two remediation rounds.

Security & lifecycle
- We accept the 30-day TTL with an audit/confirmation workflow. On expiry Redwood will provide a signed destruction confirmation and dataset checksum.
- Logs: daily access summary for the trial; full access logs available on request for up to 90 days.

Next steps (action items)
1) Catalyst to confirm final manifest and attach NDA addendum if required.
2) Redwood to send DocuSign envelope (MAP + ARA) by EOD 11/24.
3) Post-signature: Catalyst uploads artifacts and we begin the canary run per the timeline above.

For convenience, here's the HubSpot deal link and the DocuSign envelope (once it's live) in the thread metadata. Attachments we're sending with the DocuSign packet: mutual-action-plan-CAT-20261116.pdf, security-checklist-redwood-appendix.pdf. We'll also place the eval-dataset-index.csv and prompt-pack-v1.zip in the transfer package on upload.

Look forward to the trial — please confirm and we'll finalize the envelope.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
